title: 4sum
description:
Given an array nums of n integers, return an array of all the unique quadruplets [nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]] such that:

0 <= a, b, c, d < n
a, b, c, and d are distinct.
nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] + nums[d] == target

You may return the answer in any order.
 
Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,0,-1,0,-2,2], target = 0
Output: [[-2,-1,1,2],[-2,0,0,2],[-1,0,0,1]]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [2,2,2,2,2], target = 8
Output: [[2,2,2,2]]

 
Constraints:

1 <= nums.length <= 200
-109 <= nums[i] <= 109
-109 <= target <= 109

check_function:
def check(candidate):
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[1,0,-1,0,-2,2], target=0)))) == [(-2, -1, 1, 2), (-2, 0, 0, 2), (-1, 0, 0, 1)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[2,2,2,2,2], target=8)))) == [(2, 2, 2, 2)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[-3,-1,0,2,4,5], target=2)))) == [(-3, -1, 2, 4)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[-2,-1,-1,1,1,2,2], target=0)))) == [(-2, -1, 1, 2), (-1, -1, 1, 1)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[0,0,0,0], target=0)))) == [(0, 0, 0, 0)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[-5,-4,-3,-2,-1], target=-10)))) == [(-4, -3, -2, -1)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[5,5,3,5,1,-5,1,-2], target=4)))) == [(-5, 1, 3, 5)]
    assert sorted(map(tuple, map(sorted, candidate(nums=[1,2,3,4], target=100)))) == []
